part.text:
Fixed. The issue was that `@SuperBuilder` generated type parameters `C` and `B` for the builder without checking the `extends`/`implements` clauses for name collisions — so with `class A extends B`, the generated `ABuilder<C, B> extends B.BBuilder<C, B>` resolved `B` to the builder's own type variable instead of the superclass, producing the "constructor B(...) is undefined" error.

Changes:
- `src/core/lombok/javac/handlers/HandleSuperBuilder.java`: `gatherUsedTypeNames` now also collects names from the `extends` and `implements` clauses via a new `addFirstToken` helper (unwrapping `JCTypeApply` and walking to the first token of `JCFieldAccess`), so `generateNonclashingNameFor` renames the builder type params when they'd clash (e.g. `B4` instead of `B`).
- `src/core/lombok/eclipse/handlers/HandleSuperBuilder.java`: same fix for the Eclipse compiler (uses `td.superclass` and `td.superInterfaces`), plus removal of an unused import.

Verified in the container with `ant test.instance`: all 379 tests pass, including the previously failing `javac-SuperBuilderNameClashes` (the `ExtendsClauseCollision extends B implements B2.B4<Object>, B3<Object>` case), with 0 failures.
